item.text: I’m checking the current sources again before touching them. The next refactor needs to remove real friction rather than just renaming things, so I’m looking for duplication and awkward ownership across the facade, CLI, and value types.

I found two concrete problems worth fixing. The dimensions type still doesn’t fully carry its own domain semantics, and the solver still treats parenthesization as ad hoc string concatenation over raw index math; I’m tightening both now.
I’m updating the facade and solver around those semantics next. This keeps callers on the validated `MatrixDimensions` path and removes some of the remaining implicit conventions from the DP code.
The code changes are in. I’m compiling and exercising both the default CLI path and the explicit-argument path now, then I’ll pull the updated line references for a concise summary.

Refactored the API so `MatrixDimensions` now carries more of the domain logic instead of leaving it scattered across callers and the solver. [MatrixDimensions.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/019_matrix_chain_multiplication/MatrixDimensions.java:28) now has contextual parse errors, explicit `matrixCount()` / `isTrivialChain()` helpers, and the public overloads in [MatrixChainMultiplication.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/019_matrix_chain_multiplication/MatrixChainMultiplication.java:10) let callers stay on the validated type all the way through instead of dropping back to raw arrays.

I also tightened the solver internals in [MatrixChainSolver.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/019_matrix_chain_multiplication/MatrixChainSolver.java:16). It now uses the domain semantics directly for trivial-chain handling, caches `matrixCount`, and builds the parenthesization through a `StringBuilder` append path ([lines 77-95](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/019_matrix_chain_multiplication/MatrixChainSolver.java:77)) instead of recursive string concatenation.

Verified with `javac MatrixChainMultiplication.java MatrixChainSolver.java MatrixChainResult.java MatrixDimensions.java MatrixChainCli.java`, `java -cp . MatrixChainCli`, and `java -cp . MatrixChainCli 2 1 3 4`; both runs still printed `20`.
